proofPolicy: Only exhausted searches prove impossibility. State or time limits are inconclusive; no uniqueness or optimality is claimed.

checks.method: Same level with platforms: [], all ordinary rules retained.

coordinates: Source map coordinates, before centering: x=0..18, y=0..13.

hydraulicNecessity.claim: At least one deployment of the hydraulic bridge is required to finish with both heroes on the right island.
argument: The left room can only be exited across (6,4). Its trapped crate must first be extracted by a Wizard exchange, then pushed into that water cell. It becomes a fixed support, so it cannot later be reused.

The middle room can only enter the lower room across (8,6). The isolated stone at (9,6) has walls north, south and east. The sole press sends it west into (8,6), where it becomes the second fixed support. It cannot later be reused.

Only one movable crate remains. It begins on the right island at (16,10). That island initially contains one actor and no hero. Wizard exchanges preserve the total number of actors on each side of a cut: exchanging a hero with an actor on the other side cannot change the island actor count.

The optimistic geometry enumeration grants the movable NE mirror every connected supported cell, ignores actors and closed gates, and also tries every possible extra permanent support among the four water cells (12..15,10). Even with these relaxations, every mainland-to-east reflection lands at x<=14. Thus neither a hero nor a crate can be reflected directly to island x>=16 or to its last adjacent water cell (15,10).

Without hydraulics, a walk or push into the island needs support at (15,10). One remaining crate cannot be pushed there from the mainland: it sinks on the first unsupported water cell it enters. It cannot be reflected there by the computed bound. An exchange cannot create support on an empty water cell, because its endpoint must already contain a supported actor.

Creating (15,10) from the island by pushing its crate west would require both a crate and a pusher already on the island, hence at least two actors there. Before the first non-exchange arrival, that contradicts the invariant island actor count of one. Therefore no non-exchange arrival can increase the island count to the two heroes required for completion without hydraulic deployment.
limitations: This proves that the bridge mechanism must be deployed at least once; it does not claim that every individual hydraulic tile is mandatory in every solution.
The two mirror/wizard manipulations in the supplied witness demonstrate a bent swap; no exhaustive necessity claim is made specifically for a bent ray.
The bounded no-reflection searches hit their state limits and are not presented as exhaustive impossibility proofs.
